quote: subjects tended to predict 70% of the time that the blue card would occur
content: Replication check: probability matching is one of the oldest and most reliably reproduced findings in choice research, and Schul & Mayo's result is squarely in line with it: even participants who afterwards recognized that always predicting the likelier outcome was optimal failed to do so during the task. Later work bears on the essay's own hypothesis that maximizing simply does not occur to people: Koehler & James (2010) found that when the maximizing strategy is made salient, many matchers recognize it as better and matching declines. The effect replicates; its strength depends on incentives and on how visible the alternative strategy is.
